content: Chave et al. (2014) pantropical AGB allometry: AGB = exp(-1.803 + 0.944 * ln(rho * D^2 * H)) where AGB is above-ground dry biomass in kg, rho is basic wood density in g/cm3, D is DBH in cm, H is tree height in m. Pan-tropical calibration (4046 trees, 10 sites), RMSE about 14% on log scale. Preferred when height is available. Without height, use AGB = exp(-1.803 + 0.944*ln(rho) + 2.144*ln(D) + 0.207*(ln(D))^2 - 0.0281*(ln(D))^3). Site-level correction uses the environmental index E = mean annual temperature * annual rainfall * dry-season length. Allometric uncertainty: apply the recommended 25% error margin at plot scale (requirement of ForestGenius and IPCC Tier 2 reporting).

metadata.source: Chave et al. 2014 Global Change Biology 20:3177-3190

content: Chave et al. (2005) moist forest AGB allometry: AGB = rho * exp(-1.349 + 1.980*ln(D) + 0.207*(ln(D))^2 - 0.0281*(ln(D))^3). Valid for moist tropical forests (no height term). Unit: AGB kg, D cm, rho g/cm3. Use when tree height measurement is unavailable. Chave 2014 recommends site-level wet/dry correction: AGB_cor = AGB * (0.689 - 0.018*E), with E the climatic dryness index.

Phase-2 generic AGB formula (as specified in the circular-economy engine): AGB_est = exp(-1.803 + 0.944 * ln(rho * D^2 * H)) — identical in form to Chave et al. 2014 with height. Below-ground biomass via tropical root:shoot ratio: BGB = AGB * f_rs with f_rs between 0.15 and 0.22 (Central African moist forests default 0.20). Bark biomass: 10-14% of commercial trunk volume times bark density (default bark fraction of AGB 12%). Branch biomass: allocate 25% of AGB to branches, apply Biomass Expansion Factor (BEF) between 1.3 and 1.6 when converting stem-only increment to whole-plant biomass. Fine branches: D < 10 cm; thick branches: D > 15 cm.

Chapman-Richards growth model for diameter: D(t) = A * (1 - exp(-k * t))^p, where D(t) is DBH in cm at age t years, A is the asymptotic maximum diameter, k the growth rate, p the shape parameter (often 1.5-2.0). Inversion for age estimation: t = -ln(1 - (D/A)^(1/p)) / k. Undefined (asymptote reached) when measured D >= A * 0.999. Schumacher form: D(t) = A * exp(-k * exp(-c*t)). Growth-rate damping for high canopy competition: reduce k by 15-30% when Forest Canopy Density (FCD) >= 0.7 (dense forest, light-limited); increase k by up to 10% in open low-competition stands (FCD <= 0.4).

Height-diameter allometry for Central African moist forests (Northern Gabon form used in engine): H = 1.3 + 42.7 * exp(-1.426 / D), H in m, D in cm at breast height. Alternative hyperbolic form: H = 1.3 + D^2 / (a + b*D)^2 with a = 0.89, b = 0.064 (Petter et al. 2016, Cameroon/Gabon plots). Measured-height shortcut used by field crews: H ~= 4.5 m at D = 10 cm, H ~= 28 m at D = 40 cm, H ~= 34 m at D = 60 cm for canopy species. Local height-plateau below 30 m for stunted/ridge sites; cap height at 55 m.

Engone Obiang et al. (2013) diameter growth model for Okoume (Aucoumea klaineana) in Gabon: mean annual diameter increment peaks at 2.26 cm/year at DBH 21 cm, then declines. Numeric integration for age must start at recruit DBH = 5 cm (fitted domain lower bound), integrating 1/d(D) from 5 cm to measured D. For a 62.5 cm Okoume this yields roughly 40-50 years on productive sites. Above D = 45 cm, increment falls below 0.8 cm/year. The model applies within 5-70 cm DBH; outside this domain use Chapman-Richards.

metadata.source: Engone Obiang et al. 2013 Forest Ecology and Management

content: Sawdust volume estimation for field slabbing: V_sawdust = kerf_mm * A_cut_m2 / 1000 per cut, standard chainsaw kerf = 5 mm (kerf_mm=5). For a full through-cut of a log of diameter D: V = 0.005 * pi*(D/200)^2 m3 per cut. A 60 cm log slabbed into boards with N cuts yields V_sawdust = N * 0.005 * pi*(0.3)^2 approx 0.00141 m3 per cut. Bulk density of fresh sawdust ~150-200 kg/m3 (dry matter). Mycelium bio-board pasteurization: sawdust pasteurized 60-70 C for 1 hour, inoculated with Ganoderma or Pleurotus, incubation 14-21 days at 24-26 C, moisture 60-65%.
